summary.headline: EPACK Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR886 crore (+34% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 6.21% from 8.24% as PLI income dropped to nil.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose about 34% YoY to INR886 crore, the company's highest quarterly revenue, with RAC up about 44% (roughly 30% volume, 14% value). EBITDA was INR55 crore, up about 0.7% YoY, with margin at 6.21% versus 8.24%; management said the prior-year figure included INR13.31 crore of PLI income, and the like-for-like underlying margin was about 6.4% in Q1 FY26. Net profit was INR11.8 crore, and management cited a forex loss of about INR6-7 crore and higher wage costs as pressures. Management said FY27 is the last year of PLI benefit and is rolling back PLI discounts shared with brand customers, aiming to fully reverse them by year-end.

segments.name: RAC (room air conditioners)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR660 crore of the INR886 crore total; growth ~44% with ~30% from volume. Hisense JV delivered ~35,000 ACs in Q1 (~60,000 in Jan-Jun season) for ~INR65 crore Q1 revenue (~INR120 crore for the season).

segments.name: SDA + LDA (small and large domestic appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR130 crore vs ~INR80 crore last year per management; Q1 growth ~68% YoY. Gross margin reportedly 1.5-2 percentage points above AC (stated as 'basis points', likely a units slip). Washing machines: top-load fully automatic in production for 3 national/multinational brands; front-load pilot underway, mass production targeted by end-Sept/October 2026.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 23% (question-referenced figure, not confirmed by management); components are largely AC-linked (controllers, cross-flow fans, copper tubing) and seasonal. Management said growth will continue and non-AC components are being explored.

guidance_outlook: Industry AC growth expected ~20% in FY27; management expects EPACK to outgrow the industry. No formal numerical guidance given on revenue.
Target utilisation of all three plants (Dehradun, Bhiwadi, Sri City) at 55-60% for FY27 average; management said more than 60% on average.
Q2 and Q3 have historically been loss-making; management targets stopping the 'bleeding' in these quarters within 4-6 quarters, but declined to say whether Q2 FY27 will be PAT positive.
PLI discount rollback: aim to reverse fully by end-FY27; PLI ends with FY27, and normalised EBITDA expected from FY28. Prior commentary: ~6.5% EBITDA ex-PLI for recent quarters.

Capex: total budget ~INR450-470 crore; ~INR330-350 crore booked; INR60-70 crore additional capex expected in the remaining nine months; depreciation not expected to rise significantly over next three quarters.
Hisense: cumulative expected revenue of ~INR8,000 crore over five years; management said on track for calendar 2026 and front-load washing machine production by end-October.
Andhra Pradesh MoU: INR1,085 crore investment over five years, ~35 acres allotted; state investment subsidy about 50% of capex over 10 years.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR10 crore; ~INR60 crore in CWIP expected to capitalise over the next two quarters.
Sri City plant utilisation close to 50% in Q1 FY27 vs under 25% previously reported; Dehradun and Bhiwadi utilisation above 85-90% in Q1.
FY26 utilisation: Dehradun and Bhiwadi ~55%, Sri City below 25%.
Washing machine and LDA capacity ramp flagged as fastest-growing; front-load washing machine pilot to mass production around end-Oct 2026.

Compressors: management said domestic compressor capacity installed and in pipeline (operational by end-December) is sufficient; imports allowed until end of calendar 2026. No plan for in-house compressor capacity in the near term.
demand_pricing: RAC: channel inventory considered largely liquidated after old-BEE-rated stock sell-through allowed until end-June 2026; management estimates industry inventory at 3.5-4 million units, the lowest acceptable level.

Pricing: contracts with large customers reset prices quarterly; most commodity pass-through completed with a time lag, and management said little price increase remains to be passed on. Forex was the main margin headwind.

Customer base: 72 customers and 19 product categories at FY26 close; ~73 customers and 19 product lines now, targeting ~75 customers and 20 product lines by end-FY27. Three new categories added in Q1, four more in pipeline.
Commodities: no forward hedging; back-to-back booking against confirmed orders, with changes passed through in the following quarter.
Inventory: in-house inventory mix roughly 70-75% AC and 25-30% non-AC; working capital days ~50-60, with inventory elevated due to BIS/QCO revisions.

qa_highlights.question: Top 2-3 execution priorities and biggest risks (demand, regulation, competition)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to AC tailwinds continuing and faster growth in SDA/LDA (washing machines) and components, with more customers added across categories. No specific risk list was given beyond the outlook commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the ~44% RAC growth between volume and value, and whether the volume growth is anchor-customer driven?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% volume and about 14% value (AOP increases and commodity pass-through). Management confirmed the volume growth is largely from the anchor customer.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost escalation is still to be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts reset prices quarterly and the prior quarter's increase was already passed on; little remains. The main margin hit was forex, which produced a loss of about INR6-7 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory levels and working capital trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry inventory estimated at 3.5-4 million units, the lowest acceptable level. Working capital days are about 50-60, with in-house inventory still slightly elevated due to BIS/QCO revisions; the company aims to normalise it.

qa_highlights.question: Compressor supply risk as BIS/QCO relief expires around March 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports allowed until end of calendar 2026, with domestic capacity installed and in pipeline (operational by end-December) judged sufficient. No plan for in-house compressor capacity in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for depreciation, finance cost and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation not expected to rise significantly over the next three quarters. Finance cost rose about INR3-4 crore QoQ on ~40% growth, with scope to reduce via inventory normalisation. Total capex budget ~INR450-470 crore, with ~INR330-350 crore booked and INR60-70 crore more over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue and EBITDA margin outlook; PLI impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal revenue guidance; industry AC growth ~20% expected and EPACK to outgrow it. Ex-PLI EBITDA ~6.5% in recent quarters; PLI worth roughly 1-2% of margin, shared ~50:50 with customers. Management is rolling back PLI discounts with the aim of full reversal by year-end, with normalised EBITDA from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Sri City utilisation, operating leverage and FY27 utilisation target?
qa_highlights.answer: Sri City reached close to 50% in Q1 FY27 (from under 25%), while Dehradun and Bhiwadi ran above 85%. Management targets 55-60% average across the three plants for FY27, and said it is above 60% on average.

qa_highlights.question: Hisense progress and washing machine timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60,000 ACs delivered Jan-Jun season for ~INR120 crore revenue; Q1 alone ~35,000 units for ~INR65 crore. Front-load washing machine pilot underway, mass production targeted by end-October. Management said the five-year ~INR8,000 crore plan is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity hedging policy, especially copper?
qa_highlights.answer: No forward booking in anticipation of orders; back-to-back booking against confirmed orders, with changes passed through in the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 PAT positivity and structural seasonality fix, and the INR5,000 crore FY29 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 and Q3 have historically been loss-making; the company targets stopping this in 4-6 quarters and declined to guide on Q2 FY27 PAT. Top-load washing machines are in production for three national/multinational brands; management said it is largely on track for the FY29 INR5,000 crore target.

qa_highlights.question: Components revenue decline of about 23% and SDA/LDA margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the 23% figure but said components will keep growing; current components are AC-linked (controllers, cross-flow fans, copper tubing). SDA/LDA gross margin is about 1.5-2 percentage points above AC (the transcript says 'basis points'). Non-AC components are being explored.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the spike in other expenses (>50%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a forex loss of INR6-7 crore, plus higher wage costs from the 35%+ rise in sales and production value.

risks_watch: Forex losses (INR6-7 crore in Q1) and commodity costs such as copper, with no forward hedging, could keep compressing margins until PLI discounts are fully rolled back.
PLI roll-back to customers through FY27 and the end of PLI benefit: whether EBITDA moves toward ~6.5% ex-PLI and normalises from FY28.
Q2 and Q3 seasonality: whether front-load washing machine mass production (end-Sept/October 2026) and non-AC categories cut losses in these quarters; management declined to guide on Q2 FY27 PAT.
Sri City utilisation ramp (about 50% in Q1 vs under 25% in FY26) against the 55-60% FY27 target.
Working capital and finance cost: inventory still elevated from BIS/QCO revisions; finance cost up INR3-4 crore QoQ.
Compressor supply after import allowance ends in calendar 2026; BIS/QCO timing and copper QCO changes.
Capex execution of INR60-70 crore over nine months and capitalisation of ~INR60 crore CWIP; Hisense ramp versus the ~INR8,000 crore five-year cumulative plan.
key_quotes: So the entire strategy around SDA, LDA is first to neutralize the loss, and we are on track in terms of scaling up the washing machines and the other SDA businesses.

We are winning share, scaling the top line strongly and near-term profitability is being held back by the investment cycle and increase in input costs rather than by weakening in demand or competitiveness.
What impacted us most for the last quarter was especially the forex exchange rate.
So we are looking at overall utilization of all 3 plants put together at more than 60%.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand, scale and the Hisense ramp, but cautious and sometimes evasive on near-term profitability. It declined to guide on Q2 FY27 PAT or revenue numbers and attributed Q1 margin pressure mainly to forex and wage costs.
